data.name: Malekai
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Malekai is derived from the Hebrew word mālāk, which means 'my angel'. This name is often associated with the biblical figure Malachi, which means 'my messenger'. Malekai is a powerful name for a boy, symbolizing protection, guidance, and divine intervention.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the presence and guidance of angels in our lives.

in_hebrew.name: מלקאי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מלקאי הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'שליח אלוהים' או 'קריין מלך'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'מלק' שפירושו 'מלך' ו'אי' שפירושו 'אלוהים' או 'אלהים'. השם מלקאי מופיע בספר מלאכי שבתנך, שם מלאכי הוא נביא ששלח אלוהים לדבר אל עם ישראל.

in_greek.name: Μαλαχίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Μαλαχίας είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του εβραϊκού ονόματος מלקאי. Στη Βίβλο, ο Μαλαχίας ήταν προφήτης που στάλθηκε από τον Θεό για να μιλήσει στον λαό του Ισραήλ. Το όνομα Μαλαχίας σημαίνει 'αγγελος του Θεου' ή 'αγγελος του Κυρίου'.

in_latin.name: Malachias
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Malachias derivatur ex hebraico מלקאי, quod significat 'angelus Dei' vel 'messenger of God'. In Ecclesia primitiva, Malachias fuit propheta qui missus est a Deo ad populum Israel.

in_english.name: Malekai
in_english.meaning: Messenger of God or Angel of the Lord
in_english.long_meaning: The name Malekai is derived from the Hebrew name מלקאי (Malakai), which means 'messenger of God' or 'angel of the Lord'. It is associated with the prophet Malachi in the Old Testament, who was sent by God to speak to the Israelites. The name has been adopted in various Christian traditions and is often given to boys born into Christian families.

pronunciation.biblical: מלקאי (pronounced as mal-ˈkaɪ in a biblical Hebrew context)

biblical_reference.note: The prophet Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament in the Bible.
